subtitleNullable: Five FPNet checkpoints, each trained without one identity fold
descriptionNullable:
FPNet reads a mass spectrum, predicts the molecule's fingerprint [a list of yes/no structural features] and ranks the candidate structures of the right mass by how well their fingerprints match. This dataset holds five FPNet models. Each was trained without one of the five [identity-disjoint folds](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/dmitriigluzdov/casmi26-identity-disjoint-validation-folds) and without the 250 natural products of the [panel benchmark](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/dmitriigluzdov/casmi26-natural-product-panel-benchmark), so every training molecule has a model that has never seen it. On those never-seen molecules the models rank the right structure first for 68% of them (67–69% across the five folds), against 97% on molecules they were trained on: a score on seen molecules says little about new ones.

![Share of molecules whose correct structure ranks first, averaged over the five models: 97% for molecules each model was trained on, 89% for the public v4g FPNet on fold-0 molecules it was trained on, 68% for molecules of each model's left-out fold and 33% for never-seen natural products.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gluzdov-Dmitrii/Enveda-CASMI-2026/main/kaggle-datasets/casmi26-fold-safe-fpnet/seen_vs_unseen.png)

## How to use it

- **Validate without leakage.** Score molecules of fold k with model k and fit everything else on the other four folds. The public FPNet of the v4g pipeline was trained on all of them and ranks 89% of fold-0 molecules first, a number that does not carry over to new molecules.
- **Add them to an ensemble.** Averaging the standardised scores of the five models and adding half of the average to the public FPNet score of a PubChem search keeps the panel replay level with the single fold-0 model (MRR@25 0.964 against 0.965, one of 250 molecules lower); the panel is too easy to separate them, so judge such a change on new molecules or on the leaderboard.
- **Retrain on another split.** `make_split.py` builds the exclusion list for any fold and `train_fivefold.py` reproduces the training runs.

## Quick start

The example reads the dataset from either supported Kaggle mount location and prints the numbers of the figure for each model.

```python
import json
from pathlib import Path
slug = 'casmi26-fold-safe-fpnet'
D = next(p for p in (Path('/kaggle/input/datasets/dmitriigluzdov') / slug, Path('/kaggle/input') / slug) if p.is_dir())
for k in range(5):
    r = json.loads((D / f'fivefold_retrieval_fold{k}.json').read_text())
    print(f'model {k}:', {s: round(r[s]['top1'], 3) for s in ('train', 'hold', 'np')})   # seen, left-out fold, natural products
```

## What is inside

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `fpnet_fold0.pt` … `fpnet_fold4.pt` | Five models; model k was trained without the fold-k molecules and the panel natural products. |
| `split.parquet` | The 55,367 structures left out of the fold-0 model and the reason: fold 0 (55,102) or panel (265). |
| `fp_bits.npy`, `MODEL_INPUTS.json` | Which fingerprint bits the models predict and which model code loads them. |
| `train_fivefold.py`, `train_fpnet.py`, `make_split.py`, `train_fold0.log`, `fold0_history.json` … `fold4_history.json` | Training scripts, split builder, training log and learning curves. |
| `fivefold_retrieval_fold0.json` … `fivefold_retrieval_fold4.json`, `eval_ckpt.py`, `results_eval_fold0.json`, `results_eval_public_A.json` | The evaluation behind the figure, for each model and for the public v4g FPNet. |
| `check_inputs_fold0.json` … `check_inputs_fold4.json`, `input_subgroup_diagnostics_fold0.csv` … `_fold4.csv`, `FIVEFOLD_VALIDATION.json` | Checks that each model's left-out molecules were really left out and that its inputs match the original preprocessing. |
| `eval_prior.py`, `results_prior_fold0.json` | How the PubChem documentation prior changes those ranks. |
| `panel_logits.npz`, `panel_fpnet_scores.parquet`, `panel_fpnet_per_molecule.csv`, `PANEL_REPLAY_PUBLIC.json` | Cached predictions for the panel natural products and the replay of the notebook's PubChem channel. |
| `audit_public_split.py`, `SPLIT_AUDIT.json`, `identity_audit.json` | Checks that no left-out molecule is in the training set. |
| `MANIFEST_FIVEFOLD.json`, `SHA256SUMS_FIVEFOLD.txt`, `FILE_DESCRIPTIONS_FIVEFOLD.json` | File list with hashes and descriptions of the five-fold files. |

## How the evaluation works

For each molecule, up to eight spectra of one polarity are merged, and every structure of the public candidate pool within 10 ppm of its mass becomes a candidate (a median of 95). The model's predicted fingerprint scores the candidates and the rank of the right structure is recorded. The right structure is always among the candidates here, so the numbers measure ranking, not candidate coverage. Each set has 3,000 sampled molecule–polarity groups; the natural products have 499.

## How it was made

The models use the public FPNet architecture and are trained to rank the true structure ahead of nearby alternatives, with spectrum sampling, peak perturbations and mixed-precision training. Models 1–4 repeat the recipe of model 0 with the same number of training steps (82,855), one seed each. Molecules with related ring systems can still be on both sides; the scaffold folds of the identity-disjoint folds dataset separate those as well.

## Updates

- **2026-10-21:** Added the models for folds 1–4 with their learning curves, input checks and evaluations.
- **2026-10-19:** Added the model-input contract, audited panel exclusions and cached public panel comparisons.

## Licence and credits

The checkpoints and competition-derived files remain subject to the [competition data terms](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/enveda-CASMI26-molecule-id-mass-spectra/data): **non-commercial use with attribution**. The training loop and evaluation scripts are Apache-2.0; added audit/replay helpers are also Apache-2.0. Copied code and bit indices retain their original notices.

The architecture, data access and selected fingerprint bits are by [Ahmed Berat Özer](https://www.kaggle.com/code/ahmedberatozer/casmi26-v4g-inference); the bits were copied unchanged from his public candidate collection. The training kit, checkpoints and audit are by Dmitrii Gluzdov. Documentation-based comparisons use [PubChem Popularity Prior](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/dmitriigluzdov/casmi26-pubchem-popularity-prior) under its source-specific terms. Competition spectra were provided by Enveda. No new spectra or hidden-test labels were added, and panel results do not establish a competition-test gain.
